name: Starter: Irish
about: Irish in real, everyday sentences, with each one's words in Irish order.

words.bí: be (tá: is; bhí: was; beidh: will be; níl: isn't; an bhfuil: is?)
words.tú: you (thú when it is the object)
words.is: is (who or what someone is; is maith liom: I like)
words.ag: at (agam: at me, I have; againn: at us); ag + a verb: …ing
words.cónaí: living (i mo chónaí: living, where I live)
words.do: to, for (duit: to you); your (softens what follows)
words.cé: who (cé mhéad: how much, how many)
words.ar: on (orm: on me; ort: on you; air: on him or it)
words.codladh: sleep (ina gcodladh: asleep, of more than one)
words.le: with (liom: with me; leat: with you)
words.súil: eye; hope (tá súil agam: I hope)

gabh-mo-leithsceal.about: Literally take my excuse; also sorry for a small slip.

items.text: Tae agus uisce, le do thoil.
items.means: A tea and a water, please.
wrong: Tae agus uisce, do le thoil.
Tae agus uisce, le thoil do.

items.text: Dia duit! Tae, le do thoil.
wrong: Dia duit! Tae, do le thoil.
Dia duit! Tae, le thoil do.

items.text: Tá mé go maith, agus tú?
wrong: Mé tá go maith, agus tú?
Tá go mé maith, agus tú?

items.text: Dia duit! Tá áthas orm bualadh leat.

items.text: Is mac léinn í mo dheirfiúr.

items.text: Tá mé i mo chónaí i dteach beag.

items.text: Gabh mo leithscéal, cá bhfuil an stáisiún?

wrong: Gabh mo leithscéal, cá tá an stáisiún?
Gabh mo leithscéal, cá bhfuil stáisiún an?

wrong: Go raibh maith agat. Feicfidh thú mé amárach!
Go maith raibh agat. Feicfidh mé thú amárach!

items.means: I have a brother and a sister.

items.means: There's no milk in the fridge.
I was at home last night.

items.text: Is breá le mo chara ceol.

concept.line: A plain Irish sentence starts with its verb, then who: Tá an t-uisce fuar (is the water cold).
An starts many present and future yes-or-no questions and eclipses the verb (An bhfuil tú…?
After mo (my), do (your), a meaning his, ní and some other words, many first consonants soften, usually written with an h: máthair → mo mháthair (my mother), tuigim → ní thuigim (not I-understand).

words.means: agam = I have; agat = you have
the; also a yes/no question marker

concept.line: a means his, her or their, and only the change after it says which: a theach (his house), a teach (her house), a dteach (their house).

words.means: chaife = coffee (chaife: lenited singular, as in dhá chaife, 'two coffees')

concept.line: Many Irish prepositions join to a pronoun: ag + mé becomes agam (at me), ar + tú becomes ort (on you), and le + mé becomes liom (with me).

an normally means the with one thing and na with more than one, but na is also used with some singular of-the phrases; the article changes some first sounds: an t-uisce (the water), an fhuinneog (the window), na heochracha (the keys).

words.means: caithfidh = throw; spend; wear (caithfidh ...: must/have to ...)
